evidence: Cic. Lael. 103: requiēs plēna oblectātiōnis (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A favourite word of Cicero’s (Lewis & Short): whatever pleasantly fills the time. Pliny uses the plural of the turns put on at dinner, readers, musicians, clowns.

evidence: Cic. Sen. 52: requiēs oblectāmentumque senectūtis (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The thing that amuses, where oblectātiō is the amusing.
Shows to watch: games, plays, and now films and television.

terms.gloss: an entertainment at dinner (music or reading); an entertainer
terms.comment: Greek, “something heard”: the music or reading that entertained guests at table, and the performer who gave it (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: dēmus igitur aliēnīs oblectātiōnibus veniam, ut nostrīs impetrēmus
phrases.english: let us then forgive other people their entertainments, so that ours may be forgiven

sources: Lewis & Short: oblectatio · Lewis & Short: oblectamentum · Lewis & Short: spectaculum · Lewis & Short: acroama
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-plinius), checked against the editions named there.
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. entertainment, shows.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
